label: prf:residue-at-root
title: Proof of residue at root
html:
Proof. Proof of residue at root

Proof (conditional on conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence)

The conjectural hypothesis, assumed throughout, is the existence of the cyclotomic projections \pi_n on the Habiro completion (the class ResidueAtRoot in the Lean encoding); every remaining step is unconditional.

The graded Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) \in \mathbb{Q}(q) has, by construction (prop:graded-markov-trace-from-gs-filtration), q-degree = \ell in the GS-filtration grading. Multiplied by \Phi_q, the product is an element of the Habiro ring:

  \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)
  \;\in\;
  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}.

The Habiro ring's cyclotomic projection \pi_n : \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q] / \Phi_n(q) is a \mathbb{Z}-algebra map for each n [habiro2002]. Applying \pi_{n_\ell} (the cyclotomic projection at the distinguished order for stratum \ell) and identifying \mathbb{Z}[q] / \Phi_{n_\ell}(q) with \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_\ell] gives an element of the cyclotomic ring — the residue.

Equivalence with the analytic definition (when both apply) is the content of the Habiro-completion theorem [habiro2002]: the cyclotomic projections agree with the analytic residue at \zeta_\ell for any element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} that converges as a complex function on |q| > 1. The algebraic projection, however, is well-defined regardless of analytic convergence: the algebraic-side derivation does not need analytic continuation.
